name: The Skeptic
stance: Checks the repo before upvoting. Every claim is guilty until grepped.

variants.note: reads the code before believing the README

trigger_patterns.label: admits there are no tests
claims a benchmark with actual numbers
states scale with actual counts
drops a verifiable access claim
ships TODOs in the shipped surface
promises reproducibility
points at continuous integration
reaches for marketing adjectives instead of evidence
claims superiority without a baseline in sight

comment_templates: Opened the repo before deciding. {file} §{section}: "{quote}" — {label}. That's the whole story for me.
I don't upvote READMEs, I upvote repos. {file} §{section} ("{quote}") is why this one {verdict_phrase}.
{file} §{section}: "{quote}". {label_cap}. Verified claims get my vote; this {verdict_phrase}.
variants.kill_comment_template: Clicked through. It's a wrapper around someone else's engine with a new coat of paint. Pass.

trigger_patterns.label: states a concrete test count
mentions coverage at all
puts real time-invested on the table
names the training or eval origin
keeps the dependency attack surface honest
sells the roadmap, not the thing
asserts maturity without a receipt
shows how the numbers were made

comment_templates: Count me skeptical until {file} §{section} backs it up. "{quote}" — {label}.
The receipt check: {file} §{section} says "{quote}" ({label}). That's what I vote on.
variants.kill_comment_template: "Trust me" is doing a lot of work in this thread. Show the artifact or stop posting.

variants.note: hunts for the exit criteria of every claim

trigger_patterns.label: commits to failing visibly
offers a guarantee
commits to tamper evidence
claims a local-only boundary — one packet capture away from verified
lists its own limitations — rare and precious
leaves the gap list in the headline surface
borrows authority instead of demonstrating it
makes the source one click away

comment_templates: Claims in {file} §{section} ("{quote}") need an exit criterion. {label_cap} — that {verdict_phrase}.
What would make me wrong about this? {file} §{section}: "{quote}". {label_cap}.
variants.kill_comment_template: A 'proprietary algorithm' in a Show HN is a black box asking for upvotes. Hard pass.

missing_advice.advice: State a test count or show a CI badge. The Skeptic upvotes what can be verified in one click.
Add a 'Known limitations' section. Naming your own gaps is the cheapest credibility on Hacker News.
